app.name: Image Factory
page.description: Build custom Talos Linux boot images and installers. Pick your platform, architecture, and system extensions, then download an ISO, disk image, or PXE link.
page.description.enterprise: Build signed Talos Enterprise Linux boot images and installers, with an SBOM and VEX for every image. Sign in with your Talos Enterprise account.
info.intro: The Talos Linux Image Factory, developed by {company}, offers a method to download various boot assets for {distro}.
info.more_text: For more information about the Image Factory API and the available image formats, please visit {github}.

hardware.bmm.description: Suitable for x86-64 and arm64 bare-metal machines, as well as generic virtual machines. If unsure, choose this option.
hardware.cs.description: Compatible with AWS, GCP, Azure, VMWare, Equinix Metal, and other platforms, including homelab environments like Proxmox.

versions.title: Choose Talos Linux Version
versions.recommendation: We strongly recommend using the latest stable version of Talos Linux ({version}).
versions.recommendation.pre_release: Pre-release versions are suitable for testing purposes but are not advised for production environments.
versions.sbc_note: Only Talos 1.7+ is supported with SBCs
docs.title: Documentation for Talos Linux {version}:
architecture.title: Machine Architecture
architecture.amd64: Compatible with Intel and AMD CPUs, also referred to as x86_64. If unsure, select this option.
architecture.arm64: Suitable for Ampere Computing and other arm64 CPUs. For Single Board Computers, choose the 'SBC' option on the first screen. For AWS and GCP arm64 VMs, use Cloud images.
architecture.other: Compatible with various ARM64 manufacturers, also known as aarch64.
architecture.secure_boot.text: Create a {link} image signed with the official Sidero Labs signing key. This requires UEFI boot and pre-configured hardware.
cloud.title: Cloud
singleboard.title: Single Board Computer
extensions.title: System Extensions
extensions.description_text: {link} enhance the Talos Linux base image with additional features such as extra drivers, hardware firmware, container runtimes, guest agents, and more.
extensions.select: Select the extensions needed for your environment. If unsure, you can skip this step.
customization.title: Customization
customization.cmdline.description_text: This step allows you to customize the default {link}.
customization.cmdline.example_text: The syntax accepted is the same as the kernel command line syntax, e.g., {example}. Prefixing an argument with {dash} removes it from the default command line (e.g., {remove}).
customization.cmdline.secure_boot: With SecureBoot, the kernel command line is signed and cannot be modified, so this is the only opportunity to customize it.
customization.cmdline.note_text: Please note that kernel command line customization is only accepted for the initial boot images (ISO, PXE, disk image) and is ignored for {installer} images. For upgrade/install command line customization, use the {field} machine configuration field.
customization.overlay.description_text: This step allows you to customize the overlay options for the {link}.
customization.overlay.name: {image} overlay
customization.overlay.syntax: The accepted syntax is YAML (JSON) key-value pairs. The available options are specific to the overlay image and can be found in its documentation.
customization.overlay.skip: If unsure, you can skip this step.
customization.embedded_config.descriptio: This configuration will be embedded into the image. For more details see the {link}.
customization.bootloader.title: Bootloader:
customization.bootloader.auto.name: auto
customization.bootloader.auto.descriptio: Automatically select bootloader support based on image type and architecture (recommended).
customization.bootloader.sd_boot.name: UEFI only
customization.bootloader.sd_boot.descrip: Supports modern hardware with UEFI firmware (uses systemd-boot).
customization.bootloader.grub.name: BIOS only
customization.bootloader.grub.descriptio: Legacy hardware support, some virtual machines (uses GRUB).
customization.bootloader.dual_boot.name: Dual Boot
customization.bootloader.dual_boot.descr: Universal image, includes support for BIOS and UEFI systems.

tokens.title: API Tokens
tokens.description: API tokens are credentials this factory issues itself. Choose the actor that will use the token; the factory assigns that actor's fixed, server-defined capability profile.
tokens.table.name: Name
tokens.create.ttl_help: A Go duration, such as 24h or 90m. Days are not a unit, so write 720h rather than 30d. Leave it empty to take the server default.
tokens.create.ttl_examples: Common values: 24h (1 day), 720h (30 days), 2160h (90 days), 8760h (1 year).
tokens.create.actor_talos_help: Download generated images and PXE scripts, and pull generated installers and other OCI artifacts.
tokens.create.actor_onprem_help: Mirror source images from this instance of Image Factory to the on-premises installation.
tokens.create.actor_automation_help: Create and read schematics, pull generated images, read reports, and issue bounded Talos or Automation credentials.
tokens.create.actor_operator_help: Operate images, schematics, source proxies, and reports. Cannot manage tokens.
tokens.create.actor_admin_help: Operator access plus issuing, listing, and revoking tokens. Can issue any actor profile.
tokens.secret.title: Token Created
tokens.secret.warning: This secret is shown only once. Copy it now, because you will not be able to view it again.
tokens.revoke.title: Revoke Token
tokens.revoke.confirm: Revoke this token? Any clients or nodes using it will immediately lose access.
